newsitem.title: USA: Clorox buying Armor All in $400 million deal.
newsitem.headline: Clorox buying Armor All in $400 million deal.

text.p: The Clorox Co. said Tuesday it would buy Armour All Products Corp., the nation's leading maker of automobile cleaning products, for about $400 million in a move to bolster its traditional cleaning products business.
Clorox said the acquisition of Armour All would be a "logical extension" of its well known cleaning products, which include bleach, the Pine-Sol, Tilex and Soft Scrub brands, and Brita water filters.
It noted that it expected sales of automotive cleaning products to grow faster than those of home cleaning products.

Under the agreement, Clorox will buy all of Armour All's stock at $19.09 a share. McKesson Corp., a major distributor of drugs and toiletries that owns 55 percent of Armour All, has agreed to sell its stock to Clorox, the company said.
Based in Aliso Viejo in Orange County, Calif., Armour All had fiscal 1996 sales of $186 million.

Clorox, which also makes Kingsford charcoal, Combat and Black Flag insecticides, cat litter under the Fresh Step name, barbecue sauces and salad dressing, earned $222 million on sales of $2.2 billion for the year ended June 30.
"This acquisition is right on target with our strategy of finding strong equities in new categories close in to what we do," Clorox Chairman Craig Sullivan said in a statement.
"This acquisition is a logical extension of our home cleaning expertise into a market where we will have a leading position," he added.
Under Sullivan, who became chief executive in mid-1992, Clorox has streamlined operations, bought and sold several niche businesses, and bolstered its business in fast-growing overseas markets.
Armour All has about 30 percent of the $710 million market for automotive cleaning products and about 60 percent of the lucrative segment for protectants, Clorox said.
It noted that about half of Armour All sales are to customers that already buy Clorox brands, creating an opportunity for marketing and other tie-ins.
Clorox noted that growth in car ownership and rising car prices have helped fuel sales of automotive cleaning products, since people want to protect their investment.
Clorox stock rose 25 cents to $105.50 on the New York Stock Exchange. Armour All stock was unchanged at $17.50 on Nasdaq after being halted for the announcement.
Clorox said it expected to launch its offer Dec. 2 and complete the stock purchase by year-end. It said it planned to fund the acquisition with cash and short-term borrowing.
Armour All's board of directors has recommended the offer, Oakland, Calif.-based Clorox said.
